answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks when every identity must post a refundable bond and earn influence through repeated escrowed trades with randomly chosen peers. Those peers verify signed histories; fraud or coordinated double spending burns the bond, and reputation grows only after diverse successful interactions. A whisper from one account cannot instantly lift its aliases: an attacker must finance each deposit and perform costly work long enough to reach the summit of trust, paying real capital and time while fake identities advance at glacier speed.
